clue.text: Sit next to former partner in show

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone takes a seat beside their ex during a television programme or stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The partner comes first in the answer although 'Sit' comes first in the clue: 'next to' allows either order.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something is to reveal or display it publicly, so the verb means the same as show.

indicators.note: a part of the following words is taken, so the letters sit inside that run of text

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An instruction to say a section of a speech one more time.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ECHO straddle speECH Once; 'part of speech' pretends to be the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound bounced back and heard again, and as a verb it means to say again or copy.

clue.text: Device used by writer to make a point

definitions.text: Device used by writer to make a point

blocks.clueFragment: Device used by writer to make a point
blocks.note: surface reading: a rhetorical trick an author uses to argue something
setter's reading: a gadget that literally gives a sharp tip to the tool someone writes with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Device' and 'make a point' suggest a literary technique; the point is the sharp end of a pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: This small gadget shaves wood and graphite away so that a writing implement has a fine tip again.

clue.text: City's defence full of energy, very loud

indicators.note: something full of other things holds them inside it, so the defence wraps round what follows

blocks.note: a shield is a defence held against blows
E is the symbol for energy
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A town's sports team defends with great vigour and plenty of noise from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion lands after the second letter of the defence, not in its exact middle. ff, fortissimo, is the standard music notation for very loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield is a large city in South Yorkshire in the north of England, famous for steel.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for docile loses its final letter

blocks.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
a docile animal is tame

explanation.surface: A criminal who has gone nearly gentle turns out to be a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' reads as cowardly in the surface, but here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic fowl, so it is a kind of chicken.

indicators.note: without an end, the word for profundity has its last letter cut off

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer
profundity is depth of thought

explanation.surface: A specialist gives a reply that is infinitely deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone highly skilled; adept can be an adjective or a noun meaning a master of something.

clue.text: Dynamic duo lethal in same film

indicators.note: dynamic suggests energetic movement, so the letters are set in motion and rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A deadly pair of crime-fighting partners appear together in one movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dynamic duo' reads as a phrase, but 'duo' belongs to the letters being rearranged; 'in' inside the fodder is used too, leaving only 'film' to define.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma and Louise is the 1991 Ridley Scott road movie about two women on the run.

indicators.note: one thing within another sits inside it, so the word for pro goes into the middle
resolved suggests being broken down and settled anew, so those letters are rearranged

blocks.note: seven letters to be rearranged
pro means in favour of, that is for

explanation.surface: A professional sorted out a problem in a matter of minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a professional, but it is the Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortune is bad luck or an unfortunate event, which is a kind of trouble or hardship.

clue.text: Horrified husband in story turning up on time

indicators.note: in places the word for husband inside the following word
in a down entry turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a saga is a long story
H is the abbreviation for husband
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A husband turns up punctually in some tale and everyone is appalled.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGA reversed is AGAS; H goes inside to make AGHAS, and T is placed after it, since in a down clue 'on' means below.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock, so it matches horrified as an adjective.

clue.text: Hold back stone weapon, dropping resistance

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so the weapon loses the letter standing for resistance

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds
a rifle is a firearm
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone restrains a person armed with a stone weapon as they put up less of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle a yawn or a laugh is to suppress or restrain it, which is to hold it back.

clue.text: Regret harsh tune played for primitive folk

indicators.note: a tune that is played is performed in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician is sorry about a grating melody performed for some unsophisticated listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunter-gatherers are early peoples who lived by hunting animals and foraging plants before farming arose.

clue.text: Rabble repeated phrase with force, receiving service

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the service goes inside what comes before

blocks.note: a riff is a short musical phrase repeated over and over
F is the symbol for force in physics
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the British armed services

explanation.surface: A mob chants a slogan forcefully while being waited on.
explanation.walkthrough: The service lands inside the first two pieces, just before the final letter, rather than after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff are disreputable or common people, regarded with contempt as a disorderly crowd or mob.

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over completely, so the following words are read backwards

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
people who gathered met together

explanation.surface: A radical piece of art quickly gained momentum.
explanation.walkthrough: OP and MET together are reversed as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed of a piece of music or of activity in general, matching pace as a rate.

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are set out differently

blocks.note: ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A staged piece of pretence put on by someone who tells untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical describes behaviour that is exaggerated and showy, as if on stage, so it matches dramatic.

indicators.note: something eating takes food inside itself, so one word swallows the other letter

blocks.note: to dislike strongly is to hate
s is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes having a second helping wolfs their meal down quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is excessive speed or urgency of action, the same noun sense as hurry.

clue.text: Incisive tips from tipster with charm

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
to charm someone is to enchant them

explanation.surface: Sharp racing advice comes from a tipster who has charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like betting advice from the tipster, but it means the word's two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant comments are sharp and penetrating, cutting to the heart of a matter, just like incisive ones.

blocks.note: to commit a crime is to carry it out
a tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on

explanation.surface: Instructions for a craft job: perform the task using a peg and a plank of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a plank to go with the peg, but it is a governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee is a group of people appointed to manage or decide matters, like a board of directors.

indicators.note: what inhabits a place lives inside it, so those words go within the trailer

blocks.note: a trailer for a film is an advertisement, an ad
a band is a group of musicians
one is a number

explanation.surface: A rowdy pop group and their song live in a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a trailer here is a film advert, not a caravan towed behind a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned behaviour is uninhibited and unrestrained, which is one sense of wild.

blocks.note: nick is British slang for steal
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A thief pockets an item from Spain together with some money.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is the American and Canadian five-cent piece, a coin named after the metal.

blocks.note: first meaning: straight, without anything between
second meaning: to instruct or command, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an urgent command; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means straight with no intermediary, and as a verb it means to instruct someone.

indicators.note: a wandering thing strays from its course, so the letters move out of place
catching means holding on to, so the rearranged letters take something inside

blocks.note: four letters to be rearranged
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cricketer whose attention drifts fails to take a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-on is a cricket fielding position near the bowler on the leg side, and the player stationed there.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the player standing at mid-on is one of the fielding side, so a fielder.

clue.text: Be resistant to pressure during dance

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one item sits inside the other

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish country dance
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone holds out against being pushed onto the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric that repels water resists it, and to repel an attack is to withstand or fight it off.

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for knowledge goes round the island

blocks.note: lore is traditional knowledge
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Local tales about an island in the middle of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing through the valley known for its chateaux.

clue.text: Crumbs cleared by old cleaner finally in passage

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: crumbs and cor are both British exclamations of surprise
a place cleared of something is rid of it
O is the abbreviation for old
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Bits of food are swept up by a retired cleaner at the end of a hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs' looks like bits of food, but it is an exclamation, like 'cor' or 'blimey'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corridor is a long narrow passage in a building with doors leading off it into rooms.

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A little one's playground slide.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as possession but stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is an uncontrolled sideways slip of a vehicle or a person on a slippery surface.

clue.text: Fraud with ton in secret stack

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the pair of words that follows

blocks.note: a confidence is a secret told in trust
a rick is a stack of hay or straw
t is the abbreviation for ton

explanation.surface: A swindle involving a heavy weight hidden in a concealed pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret' reads as an adjective describing the stack, but it is a noun: a confidence is something told in trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence trick is a swindle in which a trickster first gains a victim's trust, so it is a fraud.

clue.text: Store of food some shared, rallying round

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used
turning round means the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Provisions are split between people who are pulling together.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, shaRED RALlying holds the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard where food is kept, so it is a store of food.

blocks.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
to complete something is to end it

explanation.surface: Put on a full tale in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' looks like a verb for putting on a play, but it is a noun: a part of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale handed down, popularly regarded as historical but not verified.
